payload.report: The patient’s prolonged respiratory symptoms, fever, lymphadenopathy, chest CT showing anterior mediastinal cavities and bilateral lower lung nodules, and biopsy revealing large atypical cells with mitoses and vascular/adipose infiltration strongly point to a malignant lymphoid neoplasm. The pathologist’s interpretation of aggressive B-cell lymphoma is central: it directly supports this hypothesis and largely excludes chronic infection and autoimmune disease, while refuting peripheral T-cell lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and other non-lymphoma malignancies. Although CD20/Ki-67 immunohistochemistry is still pending, the existing evidence and graph consistently converge on aggressive B-cell lymphoma as the leading diagnosis; DLBCL is the most likely subtype once IHC confirms B-cell lineage. Therefore the current best conclusion is aggressive B-cell lymphoma.
